what_happened: The operator hand-committed docs/design/job-planning.md without running the policy tests. The file contained three words that Athena's boundary test forbids, because they name who runs Athena. The test then failed for every job. Job 20261017-182453-a5sf was rejected because of it, although the producer's change was not at fault. The operator removed the three words by hand, and the policy tests now pass (9 of 9).
cause: Direct commits to the main line are not gated by the policy tests. Only jobs are checked, and the check runs when the next job starts. A hand commit's breakage therefore surfaces later as a failure in an unrelated job. The failed job has no baseline to show the failure predates it. Nothing ties a hand edit to the test suite, so correctness depends on the operator remembering to run the tests.
prevention: Run the policy tests on every commit that reaches the main line, not only inside jobs. Use a pre-commit or pre-push hook plus a required CI check, and reject any commit that fails. Separately, when a job's check fails, re-run the same check on the unmodified base commit. If the base also fails, flag the job as blocked by a pre-existing failure and do not reject it as the job's fault.
proposed_request: Make the policy tests, including the boundary test, run automatically on every commit pushed to the main line, whether it comes from a job or from a hand commit. A commit that fails them must be blocked, and the failing test must be named in the message. When a job's repo check fails, Athena must also run that check on the job's base commit. If the base commit fails the same check, Athena must report the job as blocked by an existing failure instead of rejecting it as unmet. Show this works with a test that commits a forbidden phrase and sees the commit blocked, and with a test where a job on a failing base is reported as blocked.
